trial_court: Metropolitan Magistrate, Traffic Court - II, Bengaluru (Crl.Misc.No.62/2016)
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner seeks protection order, residence order, compensation order, maintenance order and other reliefs from respondent after alleged physical and verbal abuse.

legal_principles.principle: The law presumes in favour of marriage and against concubinage when a man and woman have co-habited continuously for long time.
legal_principles.held: But the presumption can be rebutted by leading unimpeachable evidence.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

legal_principles.principle: An electronic record by way of secondary evidence shall not be admitted in evidence until the requirements under Sec.65-B are satisfied.
legal_principles.held: Thus, in the case of CD, VCD, chip etc the same shall be accompanied by the certificate in terms of Sec.65.B obtained at the time of taking the documents, without which the secondary evidence pertaining to the electronic record is inadmissible.

outcome.final_order: The court granted the petitioner's petition seeking monthly maintenance of Rs.15,000/-, compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-, legal expenses of Rs.25,000/- and directed the respondent to return Rs.8,00,000/- taken from the petitioner.
